plan.curriculum: Design and Technologies, Levels 5 and 6: producing a design safely using suitable materials, joins and tools, then testing and improving it; Economics and Business, Levels 5 and 6: using resources to make a product
plan.shape: 15 minutes explicit, 40 minutes build: kid inventors on BTN who tested for six months, build-test-fix on Pocket Pal, choosing a join, a quick round, then the first build
plan.criticalFeature: a prototype is built to be tested; when a test fails, fix the part that failed, don't throw out the idea
decisionPoints: the choice check: the best fix for a failed test
the exit board: a test and a fix for a new product
plan.anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 4? Say: your team's business plan lists every resource and who brings it. Read it with your team before you build.

studentTools: Each team's business plan from Session 4
manipulatives: The junk tubs and everything teams brought from home
Masking tape, scissors, string, staplers, split pins, needles and thread
A hot glue station away from the walkways: a parent helper if one has offered, or you run it in two 5-minute windows
The Pocket Pal model and the old jeans for the I Do
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Build. Test. Fix. written large on the board
Safety rules on the board: hot glue at the station only, scissors walk point down, clean-up at 5 minutes to go
videos: BTN Card Game Creators (2024, 3 min 25 sec): three students invent Swipee, test it for six months, then sell it (abc.net.au/btn/classroom/card-game-creators/104244662)

example.prompt: Join a bottle lid to a cardboard box. Which join?
steps: What are the materials? Plastic and card.
Does it need to be strong? Yes, it holds weight.
Hot glue holds plastic and card strongly, at the adult station.

example.prompt: Label one part of Pocket Pal.
steps: Name the part: the strap.
What is it made from? A jeans belt loop.
How is it joined? Sewn on.

items.prompt: Sketch your prototype. Label each part, what it is made from and how it is joined.
items.answer: A labelled sketch: each part named, its upcycled material and its join.

items.prompt: List three parts of your prototype.

example.prompt: Pocket Pal test: hang it, put a hat and a bottle in. The strap rips. What now?
steps: What failed? Only the strap.
Why? One thin layer, one row of stitches.
Fix that part: double the strap and sew it twice.
example.answer: Keep the idea; make the strap stronger.

items.prompt: Test your prototype. Write what happened and your fix.
answers: e.g. hang it with a full bottle
add a second loop of string
e.g. drop it from desk height

items.prompt: Leo's team taped a drink holder with masking tape. It fell apart when it got wet. Find their mistake and fix it.
items.answer: The idea is fine; the join failed. Fix: use hot glue or stitches, which hold when wet, then test again.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: use strong shapes to make your prototype tougher.
resources.title: Extension: Make It Stronger
resources.subtitle: Engineers make weak materials strong with clever shapes.

sections.title: Strong shapes
sections.intro: Thin card bends easily. Folded into a triangle tube, or layered three times, the same card becomes much stronger.

example.prompt: A flat piece of card can't hold up a book. How could the same card hold it?
steps: Flat card bends under weight.
Fold it into a triangle tube: triangles don't squash easily.
Stand two triangle tubes under the book.
example.answer: Fold the card into triangle tubes.

items.prompt: Why is a triangle tube stronger than a flat sheet of the same card?
items.answer: The triangle shape spreads the weight down its sides and can't squash flat, so it doesn't bend.

items.prompt: A bird house on a pole keeps tipping in the wind. Which change helps most?
items.explain: A wider, heavier base. It lowers the weight and spreads it out, so the wind can't tip it.

example.prompt: How could you test whether a cardboard shelf is strong enough?
steps: Decide what it must hold: three books.
Add one book at a time and watch.
Record when it bends, then fix that part.
example.answer: Add books one at a time and record when it bends.

items.prompt: Plan a fair test for your team's prototype. What will you add or do, one step at a time?
items.answer: e.g. Hang one more item each time until it slips; record how many it held.

slides.notes: Build day one. One line: today every team builds its prototype, tests it, and fixes what breaks.

Hot glue station away from walkways: a parent helper if one has offered (the Family Note asked), otherwise you run it in two 5-minute windows. Junk tubs from the homerooms out. Cue the BTN clip. Print the Worksheet one per team, plus a few Extension and Supported copies. 5 minutes for clean-up.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning how designers build and test a prototype.
successCriteria: I can explain what a prototype is.
I can choose a strong join for my materials.
I can test our prototype and plan one fix.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today you stop planning and start building.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Fifteen minutes with me, then forty minutes of building. Let's be quick.
notes.prep: 15 minutes explicit, 40 build. SC1 what a prototype is, for all; SC2 joins is the core; SC3 test and fix. Anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.

slides.title: Six months of testing
slides.prompt: Watch on BTN: Card Game Creators

notes.answer: they spent six months testing and improving before selling it
beats: PLAY the BTN story from the link, 3 min 25 sec.
SAY: Watch what these three students do between inventing and selling.
ASK: What did they do before they sold their game?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: they tested it, changed the rules, made demo packs
SCAN for testing and changing.
80%+ -> cold call one pair: why not sell it straight away?
Less -> replay the part about the rules, re-ask.
ASK: Thumbs: will your prototype work first time?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: mixed, which is fine
trap: thinking good inventors get it right first time.
Fix: ask how long they spent changing the rules, student says six months.
notes.prep: Launch. Ben, Sam and Jacob invented Swipee in 2022 and refined it for six months before selling.
notes.sources: BTN Classroom, Card Game Creators, 20 August 2024.

slides.label: Turn and tell: what did they do before they sold it?

slides.meaning: A first working model of a product, built to test and improve.
slides.example: Our first Pocket Pal is a prototype. We test it, then make it better.

notes.answer: a first working model, built to test and improve
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Prototype. Say it with me. Pro-to-type.
SAY: A prototype isn't the finished product. It's the one you test.
You only need one, and it needs to work.
ASK: Does a prototype have to be perfect?
10 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: no
ASK: How many prototypes does your team need?
5 sec. Cue: fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: one
trap: Fix: make it work first, make it pretty in Week 7.
notes.prep: One key word. Each team makes one prototype for Shark Tank Day, not a batch to sell.

slides.title: Build. Test. Fix.
slides.label: Fix the part that failed. Keep the idea.

notes.answer: fix the strap that failed; keep the idea
beats: HOLD UP the Pocket Pal.
SAY: I built it. Then I tested it: hat in, bottle in, hung on a hook.
SAY: The strap ripped. I felt like giving up.
But the pocket worked. Only the strap failed.
ASK: Do I throw out Pocket Pal, or fix the strap?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: fix the strap
ASK: It held. Does Pocket Pal pass the test now?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
trap: a team scrapping its idea after one failed test.
Fix: ask which part failed, team fixes only that part.
notes.stretch: What test would show Pocket Pal can hold a heavy lunchbox?
notes.help: Point to each picture: build, test, fix. Student says one step each.
notes.prep: The model for SC3. Critical feature: a failed test points to one part; fix that part.

slides.title: Choose the join
slides.label: Test with tape. Build with the strong join.

notes.answer: match the join to the materials and the job
beats: POINT to each row.
SAY: Tape is for testing. When you know where a part goes, use the strong join.
SAY: Pocket Pal is fabric, so I sewed it.
If I'd used tape, it would have peeled off the first day.
ASK: Which join for a wheel that has to spin?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: split pin
trap: Fix: ask what happens when it's carried or wet, team picks a strong join.
notes.stretch: Which join would you use on fabric and card together, and why?
notes.help: Point to the Best for column and match it with the student's material.
notes.prep: The model for SC2. Hot glue is adult-supervised at the station, never on desks.
notes.care: Hot glue burns. Parts go to the station; the helper or you run it.

A bottle cap onto a cardboard box
items.answer: Hot glue - plastic and card, at the station

items.answer: Split pin - it lets the arm move

say: Quick round. Write the best join
trap: Fix: ask whether it must last until Shark Tank Day, student picks again.
notes.stretch: Name a second join that would also work, and which is better.
notes.help: Keep the join table up while students answer.
notes.prep: First decision point: matching joins to materials. Brisk, one line of feedback each. SC2. Five items, about 4 minutes.

slides.title: The test failed. What now?
slides.prompt: A phone stand tips over when the phone goes on. Point to A, B or C.

options.misconception: fixes how it looks, not the part that failed

options.text: Make the base wider and heavier
Throw it out and start a new idea
options.misconception: thinks a failed test means a failed idea

notes.answer: B - fix the base, the part that failed
beats: SAY: Find the part that failed first.
ASK: What's the best fix?
15 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: B
SCAN pointing fingers, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one B: why not C?
Less -> back to the Pocket Pal strap, re-ask.
REVEAL after fingers are scanned.
SAY: B. The base failed, so fix the base. Keep the idea. Tick or fix.
trap: choosing C because the stand didn't work.
Fix: ask which part failed, student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Second decision point. Under 80% means stop each team at its first failed test and ask: which part?

slides.title: Build your prototype
slides.task: Build your prototype from your business plan. At 30 minutes, test it. Write what happened and plan one fix.
slides.frame: We tested ___. It ___. Our fix is ___.
slides.extendedTask: a first working prototype, tested once, with a test and fix recorded

notes.answer: a working prototype, one test, one planned fix
beats: SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Everyone, together, on three: Build. Test. Fix.
TIME 40 minutes. At 30, stop everyone.
ASK: Thumbs: has your team tested it yet?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
CIRCULATE. Ask: which part failed? What's your fix?
TIME at 5 to go: clean up, name on the prototype, store it.
trap: Fix: test first. Decoration waits for Week 7.
notes.stretch: Extension: strong shapes and a fair test.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture choices and test-fix frames. Plan the first join together.
notes.prep: Store prototypes safely with team names. Week 7 finishes the build and adds marketing.
notes.care: Hot glue at the station only: the helper, or you in two 5-minute windows.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A cardboard bird house goes soggy in the rain.
Write one test you'd do and one fix.

notes.answer: e.g. test: spray it with water; fix: cover the roof with an old plastic bag
beats: SAY: A new product. Work on your own.
ASK: Write one test and one fix.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a water test and a waterproof fix
RECORD who writes start again or paint it.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC3 on a new product. One board per student.
